drivingQuestion: Do the Rabbis disagree with R' Eliezer b. R' Tzadok?
outcomeNote: the first proof is deflected; Shmuel's ruling shows the Rabbis disagree

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: כֶּתֶם אָרוֹךְ — מִצְטָרֵף, טִפִּין טִפִּין — אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין. מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק — לְמָה לִי צֵירוּף? הָאָמַר ״מָשׁוּךְ כֹּל שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא״!
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear» a resolution from a baraita: «An elongated stain combines» with other elongated stains, so that if together they form the area of slightly more than a bean the woman is impure. But «a series of drops do not combine» to constitute a stain that renders her impure. «Whose» opinion is stated in this baraita? «If» it is the opinion of «Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, why do I» need «a combination» in the case of an elongated stain? «Didn’t he say» that «an elongated» stain of «any» size renders her «impure?»

segments.he: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבָּנַן, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ פְּלִיגִי? לָא, לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק, וְכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק — בְּעֵד, אֲבָל בְּכֶתֶם — לָא.
segments.en: «Rather, is it not» the opinion of «the Rabbis,» and should one not «conclude from it» that the Rabbis «disagree» with Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok? The Gemara responds: «No, actually» the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, and when Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said» an elongated stain is ritually impure he was referring to a stain found «on an examination cloth; but with regard to» a regular «stain» of an elongated shape, he does «not» hold it is impure regardless of its size.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק. הֲלָכָה — מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear, as Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said:» The «halakha» is «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok.» Since Shmuel rules that the «halakha» is in accordance with his opinion, it may be derived «by inference that» the Rabbis «disagree» with his opinion, as otherwise there would be no need for a ruling of halakha. The Gemara affirms: Indeed, «conclude from it» that this is correct.
